name: Tusla Fostering: national enquiries (Tusla, the Child and Family Agency; An Ghníomhaireacht um Leanaí agus an Teaghlach)
coverage: Ireland (the State foster care service; national enquiry team)
notes: Tusla is the only State fostering service. The Register your interest page links to a Microsoft Forms enquiry form; we did not read its questions because the form is drawn by script. Every fostering page also offers a national freephone line, an email address and online information sessions (one was listed for 24 November 2026). fostering.ie redirects here. A separate form is for carers moving from another provider. Tusla's May 2026 booklet lists six steps: enquiry, checks, pre-approval training, assessment, foster care committee, then matching.

name: Tusla National Adoption and Tracing Service: adoption information
coverage: Ireland (domestic and intercountry adoption; local offices listed by county)
notes: People apply through their local Tusla adoption office (rows below). The assessment page says assessment takes at least 18 months and includes interviews, home visits, a medical examination and Garda vetting (police check). The intercountry page lists eight stages, from an information meeting to registration with a mediation agency.

name: Adoption Authority of Ireland (Údarás Uchtála na hÉireann)
coverage: Ireland (independent statutory body; central authority for intercountry adoption)
notes: Information only for people thinking of adopting. It sends them to their local Tusla adoption service or an accredited body. It issues declarations of eligibility and suitability and makes adoption orders. Its accreditation page lists Barnardos, Helping Hands and Pact as accredited partners. Search results describe Barnardos' accredited service as information and tracing, so it has no row here (unverified).

name: gov.ie: Become a foster carer (Department of Children, Disability and Equality)
notes: Information only. gov.ie refused our reader (HTTP 403), so this row rests on search results. They show the page says getting in touch with Tusla is the first step, through its online enquiry form or the local area office.

name: Irish Foster Care Association (IFCA)
coverage: Ireland (national association of foster and relative carers, with local branches and hubs)
notes: Supports foster families; it does not approve carers. Tusla describes it as the national organisation that supports foster families, with a helpline, advocacy and counselling. Tusla and some agencies pay a year's membership for their carers.

name: Orchard Fostering (Orchard Children Service Ltd)
coverage: Ireland (nationwide; head office in Dublin, with call lines for Dublin, Cork, Galway and Wexford)
notes: Non-statutory agency approved by Tusla, set up in 2008 and part of Orchard Care Group. The Apply Today form asks for name, county, phone, email, whether there is a spare bedroom, children in the home, how the person heard, a call-back day and time, a message and a box to confirm being over 25. Its pages ask for applicants over 25 with a spare bedroom, a full driving licence and flexible work; couples together 3 years and living together 1 year; a youngest child of at least 3. It says the process usually takes about four months.

name: Origins Foster Care
coverage: Ireland (nationwide; offices in Dublin and Cork)
notes: Non-statutory agency approved by Tusla, working in Ireland since 2018 and owned by two practising social workers. The form asks for name, email, phone, whether the person is over 25, whether there is a bedroom for a child in care, the ages and number of children in the house, best times to call, where the person lives and a message. Its criteria: over 25, a room for each child, a full driving licence (with some flexibility in cities) and a two-year gap between a carer's own child and the child placed. It will not place a child under 5 in a home where someone smokes or vapes.

name: Five Rivers Fostering (Five Rivers Ireland)
coverage: Ireland (nationwide; offices in Dublin for Leinster, Cavan and Monaghan, in Cork for Munster, and in Co. Donegal for the north-west)
notes: Non-statutory agency approved by Tusla, founded in 2002. It says it was the first independent fostering agency in the Republic and is a social enterprise that puts all funds back into its work (unverified, so the operator type may need checking). The application form asks for name, phone, email, county, any earlier application, how the person heard, a short summary of the family, willingness to complete Garda vetting and the best hour to call on weekdays. Other forms request an information pack or ask a question.

name: Foster Care Ireland
coverage: Office in Santry, Dublin; the pages read do not say which areas it serves
notes: Non-statutory agency approved by Tusla, a subsidiary of Sorcha Homes Ltd, working since 2016 (Tusla monitoring report). The enquiry form asks for name, address, email, mobile, date of birth, relationship status, ages of children and comments. Applicants must be over 25 and have a spare bedroom. It aims to finish the assessment within 16 weeks, with at least eight visits, Garda vetting, medical reviews and two referees. The report goes to the local area foster care committee.

name: Fostering First Ireland
coverage: Ireland (receives referrals from all Tusla regions)
notes: The agency's robots.txt asks automated readers to stay out, so we did not read its pages. This row rests on search results and Tusla's 2025 monitoring report, which says it was set up in May 2005 and is part of Key Assets International. A local news article quoting the agency says the first step is an enquiry through its website, then information and an online information evening. Another says applicants must be over 25.

name: Helping Hands Adoption Mediation Agency (HHAMA)
coverage: Ireland (intercountry adoption mediation; office in Cork)
notes: Accredited by the Adoption Authority to mediate intercountry adoptions; set up in 2005. The Authority's guide says to pre-register with it during assessment and register once a declaration is granted. The contact form asks for name, phone, email, address, the adoption query, country of choice, declaration date, the gender approved to adopt and additional needs in the home study. Legal form not confirmed: search results show it trades as a limited company and once had HSE funding.

name: Pact (adoption services)
coverage: Ireland (the pages read set no area limit); office in Rathfarnham, Dublin
notes: Registered charity accredited by the Adoption Authority, founded in 1952 as the Protestant Adoption Society. It carries out domestic infant, stepfamily and intercountry adoption assessments and runs a short-term pre-adoptive foster service. For domestic adoption it tells people to start with their local Tusla adoption office. Its contact page offers phone, email and a form we could not read.
